paper_of_week.headline: Reverse diffusion theory finally meets first-order optimality guarantees for training
paper_of_week.summary:
The work tackles the longstanding mismatch between diffusion‑based sampling and optimization theory, asking when a reverse diffusion trajectory can be certified as a first‑order stationary point of an implicit loss. By recasting the reverse SDE as a stochastic gradient estimator, the authors bridge the gap and provide a convergence guarantee that mirrors classic SGD rates.

Empirically they validate the bound on synthetic mixtures and on CIFAR‑10, showing that gradient norms decay as predicted and that comparable image quality is achieved with fewer reverse steps. The results suggest that diffusion sampling can be treated as an optimizer rather than a black‑box sampler.
paper_of_week.key_takeaway: Use the paper’s gradient‑norm stopping criterion to truncate diffusion sampling without losing fidelity.

paper.title: First-Order Stationarity of Reverse Diffusions
paper.summary: Recent literature has shown a strong connection between optimization and sampling. We develop the corresponding first-order theory for diffusion models. First, the SDE-based reverse-time flows of overdamped and underdamped Langevin diffusions contract relative Fisher divergences at explicit exponential rates whenever the stationary potential of the forward process is strongly convex---a condition on the noising process one chooses, not on the data. This is a unique advantage of SDE-based reverse diffusion, absent in the reverse process based on ODEs. Second, we incorporate discretization and establish averaged first-order stationarity bounds---the sampling analog of averaged gradient-norm guarantees in nonconvex optimization---for samplers of both overdamped and underdamped diffusion models. As in nonconvex optimization, the convexity-free certificate is local: it guarantees score consistency, not global mode weights.
